source: # AeroDrive Motors: Statistical Performance & Quality Analysis (Solutions)

# View sample vector
head(eco_trim_mpg)

# Calculate mean and standard deviation
eco_mpg_mean <- mean(eco_trim_mpg)
print(paste("Eco-Trim Mean MPG:", eco_mpg_mean))

eco_mpg_sd <- sd(eco_trim_mpg)
print(paste("Eco-Trim Standard Deviation:", eco_mpg_sd))

# One-Sample T-Test
eco_benchmark_test <- t.test(eco_trim_mpg, mu = 35.0)
eco_benchmark_test
**Interpretation**: If $p < 0.05$, we reject $H_0$ and confirm that the Eco-Trim engine performance statistically deviates from the 35.0 MPG benchmark.

head(sport_trim_mpg)

sport_mpg_mean <- mean(sport_trim_mpg)
print(paste("Sport-Trim Mean MPG:", sport_mpg_mean))

sport_mpg_sd <- sd(sport_trim_mpg)
print(paste("Sport-Trim Standard Deviation:", sport_mpg_sd))

# Two-Sample T-Test
trim_comparison_test <- t.test(eco_trim_mpg, sport_trim_mpg)
trim_comparison_test
**Interpretation**: Evaluating the $p$-value determines whether fuel efficiency differs significantly between engine trims, guiding market positioning.
## Task 3: Analysis of Variance - ANOVA (Plant-wise Battery Durability)

head(factory_battery_data)

# One-Way ANOVA
anova_battery_results <- aov(lifespan_months ~ plant, data = factory_battery_data)
summary(anova_battery_results)
**Interpretation**: A significant result ($p < 0.05$) implies at least one manufacturing plant produces battery packs with significantly different lifespans, triggering a quality assurance review.
